pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, randomized, active-controlled, multi-center; 2:1 randomization to tebentafusp vs. investigator's choice (dacarbazine, ipilimumab, or pembrolizumab); stratified by LDH status
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary: Overall Survival (OS); Key secondary: PFS, BOR, DCR by RECIST v1.1

pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, uncontrolled, multi-center; Phase 1 dose escalation (3+3 design) followed by Phase 2 dose expansion at 68 mcg
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary (Phase 2): ORR by RECIST v1.1 per ICR; Secondary: PFS, OS, DCR, DOR
pivotal_trials.result: Phase 2 expansion (n=127): ORR 4.7% (95% CI: 1.8%, 10.0%); median PFS 2.8 months; median OS 16.8 months (95% CI: 12.9, 21.3)

boxed_warning.full_text:
WARNING: CYTOKINE RELEASE SYNDROME

Cytokine Release Syndrome (CRS), which may be serious or life-threatening, occurred in patients receiving KIMMTRAK. Monitor for at least 16 hours following first three infusions and then as clinically indicated [see Dosage and Administration (2.2), see Warnings and Precautions (5.1)].

key_safety: In Study 202 (N=245 tebentafusp), CRS occurred in 89% of patients (Grade 3: 0.8%; no Grade 4/5), rash occurred in 82% (Grade 3: 18%), elevated liver enzymes (AST/ALT Grade 3+) in ~12%/8%, and Grade 3-4 TEAEs in 54%; permanent discontinuation due to AEs was rare at 3.3%.
target_moa: Bispecific gp100 peptide-HLA-A*02:01-directed CD3 T-cell engager; TCR domain binds gp100 peptide presented by HLA-A*02:01 on tumor cells while anti-CD3 scFv redirects T cells to kill gp100-expressing uveal melanoma cells

_meta.indication: KIMMTRAK is indicated for the treatment of HLA-A*02:01-positive adult patients with unresectable or metastatic uveal melanoma.
